title: Learned sparse-memory retrieval, placement, training and evaluation research

sources.notes: Paired memory-off/on capability evaluation is documented; external datasets and tier-3 agentic benchmarks remain dependencies and are not modeled as executed.
Models the E0 stage and its temporal/depth overlap proxy distinction; hidden-state collection, k-means arithmetic and numerical observations are abstract.
Models device-owned gather/reduction ordering and transfer asymmetry; allocation, synchronization and timings are measurement boundaries.
Documents materializing, fused floating-point and chunked fallback branches plus the reference-agreement gate.
Int8 per-row-scaled Triton gather/reduce is represented as an atomic quantized device gather that must match its reference; kernel scheduling and floating-point values are abstract.
Inventory covers the block-width/output-dtype/warp sweep, unsupported configuration skip, numerical rejection and rows-per-second selection.
Models reachable int4 table mode and successful reduction qualitatively; nibble layout, scale application, reference tolerance and roofline reporting are source-linked in the chapter.
Models host ownership with reduction before reduced-vector transfer; CPU and CUDA timing arithmetic is not assigned fabricated performance.
Represents E4 as a baseline observation stage. The hard-coded memory-cost projection is documented and is not modeled as a memory-enabled server run.

Models the frozen-backbone retrofit gate and healthy/unhealthy utilization outcomes; corpus fingerprinting, baseline isolation, optimizer branches, census hygiene, OOM recording and fixed-width defaults are documented.

Models independent knowledge-storage and retention outcomes. Invented facts, injected/control split, held-out template, branch-off ceiling, acquisition/control/storage formulas and optional gate are documented without asserting new results.

Models the terminal teacher-gap-reduction outcome. Same-family teacher/student loading, forward KL, alpha-paired evaluation, checkpoint output and failure preconditions are documented; no target-scale claim is made.
Core attachment, retrieval, optional gate/balancing/addressing branches, local weighted reduction, census, checkpoint-recompute handling and hook lifecycle are behaviorally abstracted.
Core device-agnostic product-key shape validation, sublinear Cartesian selection, softmax weights, weighted gather and overlap metric are behaviorally modeled.
Shell recipe has no language symbols; it enables scaled widths and the per-token gate for 9B, 4B and 0.8B runs and filters console output. Comments are historical motivation, not modeled results.
Shell recipe has no language symbols; it waits for a tagged process and runs four model rungs sequentially to avoid concurrent allocator pressure.
Shell recipe has no language symbols; it fixes c=256 while selecting d_value=d_model and d_query=d_model/2 through -1 sentinel arguments.
Shell recipe has no language symbols; it fixes data seed and varies training seed for three 9B trials. It does not itself establish stability.

assumptions: This is a standalone research branch and is not assumed reachable from the current production serving plugin.
The formal model treats tensor kernels, optimizer steps, model forwards, measurements and checkpoint writes as atomic but retains operation order, placement, modes, gate outcomes and failures.
A successful gatherReferenceMatched state means a source driver's numerical acceptance condition passed; it does not assert bitwise identity or a particular latency.
Random and k-means E0 codebooks are staleness proxies rather than evidence from a trained deployed memory.
E4 projections use source constants and are not treated as an observed memory-enabled SLO.
Knowledge storage, capability retention and teacher-gap reduction are separate observations; none implies another.
Comments describing earlier measured values or hypotheses are research provenance, not newly verified claims.
Hugging Face models and datasets, PyTorch, Triton and external benchmark checkouts are dependency boundaries, not first-party sparse-memory implementations.

implementation_checks.description: CPU inspection/differential: use a small square table and even query width, enumerate all Cartesian pair scores, and compare selected row IDs and softmax weights with select; separately confirm non-square rows and odd query width raise ValueError.
CPU differential: compare gather against an explicit weighted sum for multiple tokens, heads and repeated row indices, including normalized and non-normalized weights.
CPU source/differential check: with nonzero sel_bias, verify biased scores choose rows while returned softmax weights are computed from original scores at those chosen pairs.
CPU differential: compare embedding_bag plus head summation with an explicit per-token/per-head weighted row sum; check gate-disabled and deterministic gate-enabled residual deltas separately.
CPU autograd inspection: confirm the auxiliary addressing loss gives subkey gradients but no query-projection gradient because query activations are detached for the recomputed scores.
CPU differential: compare floating-point embedding_bag and impl_index_select outputs for repeated/random indices; this is a correctness comparison only, not an XPU performance substitute.
CPU differential: exhaust signed values -8 through 7, unpack the low/high nibble planes using the kernel's offset convention, and compare exactly with the original tensor.

CPU-oriented comparison: validate host F.embedding_bag against an explicit bf16 weighted sum, then measure pinned/pageable reduced-vector copy separately from raw-row copy; do not attribute CUDA transfer results to CPU gather speed.
Source inspection check: verify storage_effect equals injected acquisition minus matched control drift, the ceiling is measured with alpha zero, and retention remains a separate held-out CE delta.
CPU source/differential check on tiny logits: compare chunked_kl with direct forward KL, and verify gap_closed is omitted when the student-teacher CE denominator is effectively zero.
